draft.title: Marriage
card: The Marriage Act 1961 is a Commonwealth law. It sets the rules for a valid marriage anywhere in Australia.
Since 2017 the Act has defined marriage as the union of two people, to the exclusion of all others, voluntarily entered into for life. Two people of any sex can marry.
For a valid marriage, both people must freely consent and be at least 18, or be 16 or 17 with a court's approval. Neither can be already married, and they cannot be close family members.
A marriage is also formed through a ceremony. An authorised celebrant must conduct it and two witnesses must attend.
draft.remember: A valid marriage meets the rules of the Marriage Act 1961, and since 2017 it is open to two people of any sex.

a.q: Which change did the Marriage Act 1961 undergo in 2017?
opts: It allowed two people of any sex to marry
It raised the minimum age for marriage to 21
It gave each state its own rules for marriage
It ended the need for consent to a marriage
a.why: The 2017 change widened the Act so that two people of any sex can marry. Marriage law is still Commonwealth law and consent is still required, so the other options are wrong.
a.clue: The change was about who is allowed to marry.

b.q: Lena, aged 30, is already married. She holds a ceremony with a celebrant and two witnesses to marry Tom, who is single and consents. Why is the new marriage not valid?
opts: Lena is still married to another person
Lena is too old to marry for a second time
Tom and Lena did not have a court's approval
The ceremony was held without enough witnesses
b.why: A person who is already married cannot marry again, so the new marriage is not valid. The ceremony met the requirements for a celebrant and two witnesses, and court approval is only for 16 and 17 year olds.
b.clue: Check the ceremony first, then check each person's existing status.

a.best: It allowed two people of any sex to marry

b.best: Lena is still married to another person

The clue 'check each person's existing status' points straight at the answer that Lena is already married, so a student can pick it without knowing the rule.
